entityDescription:
SoftWater develops innovative methodologies and tailored software solutions to support environmental policies and foster smart and sustainable natural resources management.

Climate change risk impact analysis
We deal with climate change-related challenges, assessing the economic, social, and environmental impacts and risks (physical and transitional). We cover a wide range of case studies in terms of scale, scope, and complexity, from territorial analyses focusing on people’s safety to the risks associated with agricultural and/or industrial activities. Main competencies include handling different datasets (satellite, reanalysis, observations), statistical downscaling of regional climate data, computation of climate indicators, and exposure assessment.
Modeling complex water and environmental systems
Our modeling expertise lies in the development and application of mathematical, hydrological, and data-driven models to support decision-making, as well as in exploring solutions to multi-objective problems through evolutionary-based optimization techniques. We integrate artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to improve forecasts and predictions in the environmental fields of water, food, energy, and land. Our modeling activities leverage reliable computational libraries and include data preprocessing and harmonization, satellite image classification, statistical analyses, and data mining techniques.

Smart platforms for environmental big data
We develop lightweight, interactive web platforms that integrate spatial data, time series, and visual analytics interfaces to provide customized solutions for effective data visualization and decision support. Based on a mature, fully open-source stack, our platforms can also include integrated models, engines for computing a wide range of indicators, and AI-based procedures that run in real time to provide meaningful insights.

We pioneered the study of cosmic radiation and micrometeorite impact-induced soil/dust oxidants, as well as the monitoring and mitigation of their negative effects on astronaut health, instrumental payloads and space missions, while also leveraging some of them positively.

Our ultimate aims are:
•	Continuously prolong the presence of humans and of instruments in the space environment, and of the space missions by significantly reducing their risk, failures and costs.
•	Develop technologies that enable resilient space habitability, planetary terraforming and commercial exploitation.
•	Make use of these technologies to benefit our planet Earth: space requires high optimization in exploration which can lead to better use of terrestrial resources!

? Sensors
a)	Sensors for the main space oxidants Reactive Oxygen (examples at TRL4 , ) and Perchlorate (mainly on Mars) Species for monitoring their negative effects (oxidative, explosive, biotoxic), and for countering them by specific intervention services: on astronaut health, spacesuits, extraterrestrial life biosignatures, base space stations, spacecraft, rovers, space habitats/greenhouses, dust filtration systems, water/food supplies, equipment, and also on Earth's space and microsatellite ecosystem (for Public Health and Civil Protection from atmospheric pollution by dusts from African winds, mines, wildfires, space debris, volcanoes, exposure to UV, nuclear, and radioactive radiation, monitoring biotoxic inefficiency of air/dust filtering systems in aircraft, mining, buildings, hospitals, industries etc).

Cosmic dust and exosphere/atmosphere simulant single-process production or modification to simulate planetary environments of all kinds and with ultra-high fidelity (one-to-one replicas in texture, size distribution, physical chemistry, oxidant activation, electrostatic charge capacity and particle levitation, in cryogenic, vacuum, and mixed-gas conditions)

description:
Twin Photonics GmbH is a deep-tech SME developing scalable, chip-integrated sources of entangled photon pairs for quantum communication and networking. The company focuses on fully integrated, turnkey photonic modules that combine on-chip lasers, nonlinear generation elements, and spectral filtering to enable narrowband photon emission with precise frequency control. Our core technology is based on integrated photonic circuits (PICs) and hybrid integration.

We have demonstrated high-rate, telecom-compatible entangled photon sources with generation bandwidths exceeding 5000 GHz and pair rates above 200 kHz, while maintaining compatibility with standard optical communication infrastructure. The architecture supports frequency multiplexing via cavity-enhanced designs, enabling multiple discrete spectral channels and improved key rates for quantum networks. Twin Photonics is advancing both C-band sources for fiber-based quantum communication and other wavelengths to enable broadband interconnectability with next-gen quantum hardware. Our activities include design, and experimental validation of integrated quantum light sources, as well as system-level development for deployment in real-world quantum network environments. 

The company collaborates with leading academic and industrial partners across Europe and is actively engaged in developing next-generation quantum hardware for applications including QKD, quantum interconnects, and quantum internet.

MConnected Ltd is an Asset Intelligence company with its core skills firmly on AI and IoT principals and technologies. This “Predictive IoT” process has been very successful, leading to significant projects within the freight logistics, predictive maintenance, maritime and defence verticals. We focus on developing technologies for collecting data, whether numeric or textual, at scale, and in an automated manner that require minimal human interaction.
 
MConnected’s Technologies
MConnected’s IoT solutions operate on LoRaWAN Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWAN) that are optimised for battery life, range, indoor-outdoor coverage, bi-directionality and cost. They utilise a variety of field-based sensors, designed to send small amounts of data over long distances. Each of the sensors send their short packets of data to a gateway. MConnected’s network servers manage the data intelligence and network complexity, filtering redundant data, performing security checks and adaptive data rate management. If a sensor is mobile, no handover is required from gateway to gateway, a critical feature to enable asset-monitoring applications. The integrated platform provides an end-to-end solution that delivers insights and supports decision-making, creating value for the end-customer.
The business accommodates the full spectrum of technology requires for a complete IoT ecosystem to be delivered to our clients. The ecosystem can be simplified into discrete but well-connected silos:
 
THINGS>EDGE>GATEWAY>IoT PLATFORM>DATA ANALYTICS

entityDescription:
AMC Robotics Ltd is a UK-based early-stage company developing autonomous robotics and drone technologies to support safer, more efficient monitoring and inspection of maritime vessels, with a view to integrating satellite connectivity from the European Space Agency (ESA) for data relay, positioning, and situational awareness. The company’s core focus is on smart robotics solutions, drawing on advances in autonomous navigation, sensing, and AI to automate inspection and monitoring tasks that are difficult, dangerous, or costly for human crews. AMC Robotics aims to deploy robotic systems (surface, climbing, or aerial platforms) to inspect hulls, deck structures, cargo areas, and hard-to-access sections of vessels, reducing the need for manual rope access or dry-docking. Drone and robot payloads are designed around multi-sensor data acquisition: high‑resolution imaging, thermal and corrosion mapping, structural anomaly detection, and environmental monitoring (e.g., emissions, hull fouling, leaks). By automating routine inspection, the company targets higher inspection frequency, improved data quality, and lower operational risk for shipowners, ports, classification societies, and offshore operators.
AMC Robotics Ltd is a downstream user and integrator of space-enabled services in the maritime domain: Satellite positioning: ESA/GNSS services (e.g., Galileo) provide precise, resilient positioning and timing for autonomous robots and drones operating around large vessels, in ports, anchorages, or coastal waters, enabling accurate navigation and repeatable inspection paths. Satellite communications: ESA-enabled satellite links support near real‑time data uplink and downlink between robots/drones and shore-based systems, ensuring continuous command, control, and data streaming even beyond coastal radio coverage. Earth observation integration: AMC’s systems can be positioned to complement EO-derived insights (e.g., vessel detection, route monitoring, environmental anomalies) by providing close‑range, high‑fidelity inspection data that can validate or refine satellite observations.
The robots and drones generate structured inspection datasets that can be time‑stamped and geo‑referenced using satellite positioning, then shared via ESA satellite communication services to cloud-based platforms for analysis, reporting, and regulatory compliance. Target customers include vessel owners, charterers, ports, insurers, and maritime authorities who need evidence-based documentation for safety, maintenance planning, and environmental reporting; the ESA-enabled connectivity turns AMC’s robotic systems into a continuous, remotely accessible inspection service. In the context of ESA’s “Commercial Applications of Space-Enabled Robotics: Maritime and Port Operations” type initiatives, AMC Robotics fits as an SME delivering operational robotics and drone solutions that depend on satellite positioning and communications to unlock new data products and business models in maritime inspection and monitoring

description:
TerraViso is a geospatial technology company developing satellite-enabled environmental intelligence solutions to support land-use planning, environmental assessment, and nature risk analysis.

The company’s platform integrates Earth Observation data, machine learning, and spatial modelling techniques to generate scalable, repeatable insights on habitat classification, biodiversity condition, and land-use change. By combining satellite imagery with advanced geospatial processing, TerraViso enables consistent assessment of environmental characteristics across sites, regions, and time periods.

A key capability of the platform is the ability to support forward-looking scenario modelling, allowing users to evaluate the potential impact of land-use changes on biodiversity outcomes. This enables decision-makers to move beyond static assessments and consider future environmental scenarios in a structured and quantitative way.

TerraViso is designed to address the limitations of traditional ecological assessment approaches, which are typically manual, time-consuming, and difficult to scale. By leveraging Earth Observation data, the platform reduces reliance on field-based surveys and enables standardised, data-driven analysis that can be applied consistently across large geographies.

The technology has been developed with a focus on real-world deployment and commercial application, targeting users such as developers, environmental consultancies, local authorities, and infrastructure providers. The platform is capable of generating outputs aligned with regulatory requirements, including biodiversity assessment frameworks used in the UK planning system.

TerraViso has developed an operational platform with existing capabilities in habitat classification, biodiversity modelling, and reporting workflows, with ongoing development focused on enhancing scenario modelling, improving model accuracy, and enabling portfolio-level environmental intelligence.

The company is positioned to deliver scalable environmental intelligence services that support more efficient, consistent, and informed decision-making, with Earth Observation data forming a core component of the technology stack.

We develop innovative, AI/ML-integrated methodologies and Application Ready Data (ARD) to automate the extraction of environmental change metrics across vegetation, wetlands, permafrost, and coastal ecosystems . VDK actively collaborates with major stakeholders, including Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), Natural Resources Canada (NRCan), academia, and Indigenous communities, to translate complex SAR time-series data into actionable intelligence for biodiversity conservation and climate change adaptation
